cover_hook: 7 coat colours of one elusive wild cat, caught on camera
caption_hook: 🐆 Camera traps in India caught one wild cat species in 7 different coat colours, from gold to black + 3 more wins you missed 👇
question: Pick a colour: golden, red, grey or black? Reply with one word 🐾
share_line: Send this to the friend who loves big cats
first_comment: One camera trap caught a red and a golden cat in the same spot, possibly a pair. Which colour would you most want to see in the wild? 🐾

stories.headline: Camera traps caught one wild cat in 7 coat colours
stories.summary: Over 106 camera sites, scientists photographed Asiatic golden cats in golden, cinnamon, grey, black, brown, red and ocelot-spotted coats, all in one Himalayan district.
stories.why: It makes the Eastern Himalaya a hotspot for this cat's colours, and why it varies so much is still a mystery.

stories.headline: An 800,000-year-old elephant tooth revealed a lush ancient valley
stories.summary: A molar from a 10-tonne straight-tusked elephant, found beside stone hand axes, showed via CT scans, isotopes and pollen that early humans lived among reeds, willows and wetlands.
stories.why: The valley sat on the route between Africa and Eurasia, and stayed green through 7 or 8 ice ages.

stories.headline: A TV reporter swam into a flood to save a trapped driver
stories.summary: While covering floods, ABC journalist Will Murray saw a man stuck in his sinking car. He swam out, a local named Daniel jumped in to help, and together they got the driver out.
stories.why: Murray says having a stranger beside him in the water made him feel braver.

stories.stat_label: dogs in the US with this job
stories.headline: The Grand Canyon hired a dog to keep elk away from crowds
stories.summary: Blue, an 18-month-old Catahoula Leonberger, steers bold elk away from busy spots like the local school, without ever touching them. Rangers collared 9 elk to measure if it works.
stories.why: Fewer close calls for both visitors and elk, and Blue is a furry reminder to keep your distance.

fun_fact: The straight-tusked elephant was one of the largest land mammals of the Ice Age, weighing about 10 tonnes.
